request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Best LightGBM (run 1, 0.7346) beats logistic (run 3, 0.6925) by 0.042, below one SD (0.057-0.068), so the simpler logistic is preferred under the stated rule.
All four runs are within about 0.04 PR-AUC, with fold SD of 0.06-0.075. The differences are within noise.

ROC-AUC of about 0.94 and PR-AUC of 0.69-0.73 against a 9.35% base rate is very strong. Provider-level claim aggregates may leak the label, e.g. if the label was derived from claim patterns or size or volume features.
The PotentialFraud label origin is undocumented, so the model may reproduce a rule or heuristic rather than actual fraud.
Precision@50 is 0.756-0.772 in all runs, so the queue of about 100 is not differentiated by model. Precision@100 is not reported and is the metric that matters.
Dropping size features (no_size) barely changes results, which is reassuring against volume proxies, but the remaining money, intensity and duplication features could still encode the label.
Folds are probably random across providers. Claims span only about 13 months, so no temporal validation is possible, and fold SD is large with around 506 positives.
Only 4 runs have been tried and no logistic variants with no_size. Tuning is not exhaustive, but the gains available are small.

next_experiments.rationale: Check whether a simple, size-independent linear model matches the all-features logistic. Stronger regularization should reduce variance and leakage via volume proxies.
A heavily regularized, shallow GBM without size features tests whether the boosting edge is real and robust or just noise.
